\section{Method}\label{sec:method}
The method is a known toolkit applied to the new setting. \textbf{Factor model.} After standardisation (and, where chosen, a logit transform of scores bounded in $(0,1)$, picked per pool on the training folds by held-out likelihood in the original score space), a new model's row is modelled as $x=\mu+Wz+e$ with $z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_r)$, loadings $W\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times r}$ and independent noise $e\sim\mathcal{N}(0,D)$ with diagonal $D$ (floored at 0.05 in standardised units). $W$ and $D$ are fitted to the training rows by EM \citep{rubin1982em}; the rank $r$ is chosen by inner five-fold held-out likelihood with the one-standard-error rule. \textbf{Prediction.} Given $x_S$, the prediction of $x_T$ is the Gaussian conditional mean under $\Sigma=WW^\top+D$. \textbf{Selection.} Greedy Bayesian A-optimal selection adds, one at a time, the candidate benchmark whose observation most reduces the summed conditional variance of the targets; it needs only $W$ and $D$ and takes seconds. The target set is the one defined by the design of Section~\ref{sec:protocol}. \textbf{Comparisons.} Selectors: random (200 draws), greedy D-optimal, $k$-medoids on one minus the absolute correlation, the largest weights on the first principal component (``best one-factor''), maximum variance, pivoted QR, rank-$r$ leverage scores, and an oracle that picks the best of the sampled sets on the test targets (a bound). Predictors on the same sets: one-factor offset, ridge, $k$-NN, Ledoit--Wolf conditioning \citep{ledoit2004well} and fold-in Soft-Impute \citep{mazumder2010spectral}; the best of the first four on training rows is the ``best simple'' predictor. We call the Gaussian model the \emph{factor model}; it differs from probabilistic PCA \citep{tipping1999probabilistic} in its non-isotropic noise.
